title: Direct-image transformations are determined by inverse-image mates on associated representables
statement: Let C be a category with object universe w and hom universe v and J a Grothendieck topology. Let E be any category and a,b geometric morphisms from E to the sheaf category of sets in Type(max v w), in the sense of [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Let A=largeAssociated J be the associated-representable functor of [def-trf-large-oriented-site-data]. For every natural transformation delta:A composed with b.inverse to A composed with a.inverse, there is a unique natural transformation tau:a.direct to b.direct whose inverse-image mate at A(U) is delta(U), for every U in C. No topological subcanonicity or finite-limit assumptions on C are required. Moreover an isomorphism delta of those inverse-image restrictions extends to an isomorphism of direct images with the same prescribed mate.

proof.text: For each M in E and U in C, the sheafification adjunction and lifted Yoneda identify sections of a.direct(M) at U with maps a.inverse(A(U)) to M. Precomposition with delta(U), followed by the inverse identification for b, defines a map of sections. Naturality in U follows from delta.naturality and the naturality of the adjunction/Yoneda equivalences. Naturality in M follows from their right-variable naturality. Thus these section maps form a transformation tau of direct-image functors.

source.place: ILO XI 1.3, direct-image section construction; 1.6 uniqueness

proof.text: The conjugate-unit identity for the two adjunctions, applied to A(U), identifies the inverse-image mate of the constructed transformation with delta(U), since the unit corresponds to the identity under the Hom equivalence. For any proposed tau, naturality at a map a.inverse(A(U)) to M and the same conjugate-unit identity express its effect on the corresponding section as precomposition with its mate at A(U). Those sections exhaust all sections by adjunction and Yoneda. Hence a transformation with the prescribed mate agrees with the constructed one on every section of every sheaf, proving uniqueness.

source.place: ILO XI 1.6, determination of the direct image from Hom on associated representables

proof.text: Apply the unique-extension theorem to delta.hom and delta.inv. Mates reverse compositions and preserve identities, so the mate of either composite is the identity on each associated representable. The unique-extension theorem therefore identifies both composites with identities. These two maps define the desired direct-image isomorphism, with its mate formula inherited from the hom extension.

source.place: ILO XI 1.6, isomorphism and uniqueness of the direct-image comparison

lean.statement:
theorem largeDirectImageFromRepresentables {C : Type w} [Category.{v} C]
    {E : Type e} [Category.{ve} E] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (a b : GeometricMorphism E (Sheaf J (Type (max v w))))
    (δ : largeAssociated J ⋙ b.inverse ⟶ largeAssociated J ⋙ a.inverse) :
    ∃! τ : a.direct ⟶ b.direct, ∀ U : C,
      (GeometricMorphism.inverseMate τ).app ((largeAssociated J).obj U) = δ.app U
